answer: A credit bureau file check gives each agent one anchor. The applicant enters name, birth date and address; the bureau replies only match or no match plus an opaque file ID, and validators store a salted hash of that ID so one file opens one identity. Building a new bureau file takes years of bills and accounts, so a falcon-fast script cannot echo one person into hundreds of seats. Seen through that single prism, every clone points back to the same file and is refused. Limit: thin-file newcomers are excluded, and leaked bureau data could seed false matches.
